analysis:
The map's deepest claim about this essay is that it thinks definitionally and architecturally — What at 0.56, Formal Cause at 0.97, Insight at 0.86, Thinking at 0.98 — and that claim is almost embarrassingly correct. "Equality gives rise to challenging questions which are not altogether easy to answer": the essay opens by posing, and everything after that first sentence is the construction of an answer-machine. Even the small cells are right in their proportions. The 0.1 at the self-questioning slot earns itself: Frege's opening genuinely interrogates its own question — is equality a relation of objects or of signs? — before dissolving it into stipulation. The 0.03 for questions in the scientific lens is exactly the right calibration of Frege's method: questions are ignited in the first paragraph and never thematized again; the essay is one insight crystallized, not an inquiry sustained. What the map misses — and this is the systematic blind spot running through the whole reading — is that the essay's machinery has a destination, and the destination is where the essay's actual weight lies.

The Formal Cause reading is the map's one near-absolute judgment, and it is faithful because Frege's explanatory principle really is structural, not dynamic. Nothing in the essay happens; things are *arranged*. "The regular connexion between a sign, its sense, and its reference is of such a kind that to the sign there corresponds a definite sense and to that in turn a definite reference" — the triad is then instantiated a second time at the level of the sentence (sentence / thought / truth value), and the whole argument runs on substitution: replace a co-referential sign and the truth value is preserved while the thought changes. That homologous duplication is the essay's engine, and the numerical lens caught its shape precisely: Two at 0.46 and Three at 0.5, the dyadic puzzle (a=a versus a=b; morning star versus evening star) resolved into a triadic architecture. There is also an elective affinity worth noticing: the reading applied as given, each lens run mechanically across six slots, and this is itself the essay's method — one triad iterated across contexts, identity statements, sentences, indirect speech, fiction. A rule-machine reading a rule-machine explains why the map is so faithful on the apparatus.

But the near-zero Final Cause is wrong, and the Feeling slot at 0.0 repeats the error. The essay states its telos in its second paragraph: identity statements "have often a very valuable extension of our knowledge," and if equality were merely a relation between signs, "a = b" would express no proper knowledge at all. The entire sense/reference architecture exists *for the sake of* rescuing cognitive value from a purely referential semantics. "Erkenntniswert" is an evaluation of worth — a Feeling-function operation if ever there was one — and the map zeros it twice, in two different vocabularies. This is not a small cell: it is the reason the paper was written.

The map's best catches are its readings of the intermediate. Aether at 0.19 (alchemical) and Eternal Objects at 0.29 (processual) independently converge on the same truth: Frege's Sinn is precisely a psychoid, a pure potential. "Between lies the sense, which is indeed no longer subjective like the idea, but is yet not the object itself." The telescope analogy makes the doctrine optical — moon = reference, image in the instrument = sense, retinal image = idea — and the sense-image is repeatable, ingressible into unbounded occasions: "to a given reference there does not belong only a single sign," and the same sense is carried by signs across languages. Madhyamā at 0.54 is the best single name for Sinn in the entire map — intermediate structuring — and the Para Vāk lens also caught the essay's characteristic fold: in indirect speech, "the words have as their reference what would otherwise be their sense," speech turned back upon its own middle level. (Tellingly, the map disagrees with itself here: Epi-Logos at 0.18 registers the self-referential fold, while its sibling slot in the phenomenal lens, Introversion at 0.01, barely notices it.)

The main error is L2-3 BOTH at 0.46, glossed as "contradiction, dialetheism." The classifier was almost certainly keyed to the epigraph's "and yet" — same body, differing thoughts — and mistook the essay's generative tension for its logic. But Frege's whole maneuver is to *stratify* rather than to hold: what is same at the level of reference is different at the level of sense, and no contradiction arises because predication is level-indexed. The essay's logic is not dialetheic; it is the most aggressively bivalent logic ever written, the one that hypostatizes bivalence itself into objects — "for brevity" the True and the False. The map also scores IS-NOT at 0.03, which badly misreads the essay's texture: nearly every load-bearing sentence is discriminative negation — the sense "must not be confused" with the idea, the thought "is not" the truth value, grammar's suggestions are rejected — boundary-drawing is the paper's dominant logical operation. The tension is real; it belongs to the opening question, not to the solution, and the map has promoted the essay's problem into its verdict.

Two consequences of that same blind spot on destinations deserve separate notice. First, the monism miss. The doctrine that "all true sentences have the same reference," with the corollary that "in the reference of the sentence all that is specific has been effaced," erects a single object — the True — at the summit of the entire referential hierarchy. Every true thought anyone has ever thought co-refers to it. That is the essay's most extravagant claim, a monad of meaning, and the map assigns it 0.01 twice (One; Anuttara). Second, the Being question. Sein at 0.66 is defensible — truth values are, scandalously, *objects*, announced in a single stroke of stipulation — but the map over-credits an ontological boldness Frege performs rather than argues, and it papers over the essay's most notorious silence: whether senses themselves are objects is never settled, and the essay's Being-talk is laconic by design.

The social and temporal under-registrations are subtler. Community Integration at 0.03 ignores what makes Sinn worth distinguishing in the first place: it is the *common* property. "The sense of a proper name is grasped by everybody who is sufficiently familiar with the language"; the idea is "wholly subjective"; the telescope image, though one-sided and viewpoint-dependent, "is still objective, inasmuch as it can be used by several observers." The essay's unspoken polemic — against the reduction of meaning to private mental content — is precisely that meaning must be shareable, and the map, having caught the private/mediating side, drops the common side entirely. Similarly, Zeit at 0.05, with Paśyantī (unified seeing) at 0.07: the paradigm example smuggles temporality and vision into a theory that bans both. "Morning star" and "evening star" are literally times and ways of *being given* — the sense is the Art des Gegebenseins, the mode of appearance, perspectival and quasi-optical — while the referent is timeless. The essay hides indexicality in plain sight at the exact spot where it demonstrates the distinction.

The remaining zeros are themselves informative, because the essay's exclusions are its thought. Water at 0.0: nothing flows; signs are fixed. Svātantrya at 0: senses do not act. Winter at 0.01: nothing in the essay perishes or even anticipates its own finitude (Spring at 0.47 for the founding gesture is historically exact — this is the birth certificate of the philosophy of language). Intuition at 0.01 is fair but worth one sentence: the telescope analogy is the essay's single pictorial argument, the only place Frege trusts an image to do conceptual work, and the only narrative admitted is *Odysseus* — invoked precisely as a fiction whose reference is in doubt: because we do not know whether "Odysseus" has a reference, "we are also uncertain whether the whole sentence has one." The one story in the essay exists to mark the boundary of what logic can verify.

So the pattern of the reading as a whole: excellent on the essay's Sinn, thin on its Bedeutung. The map caught the intermediate level, the potentials, the architecture, the founding act — everything about *how* the paper means. It under-registered everything about *what the paper is about*: the True, the object itself, the epistemic value, the community of thinkers who share a sense. That is a precise asymmetry, and it is the very one the essay was written to outlaw. In Frege's own terms, a sign is answerable at both levels — it expresses its sense and stands for its reference. The reading has mastered this paper's sense of itself and given short weight to its reference; it is the error "Über Sinn und Bedeutung" exists to name.
